items.title: OpenAI counter-sues Apple over trade secret theft
items.content_html:
OpenAI has now gone on the offensive in its trade secret lawsuit, by countersuing Apple for taking secrets for itself, as well as for going after suppliers who work with both companies.

So far, the lawsuit launched by Apple against OpenAI has seen Apple take on the AI company after former Apple employees defected, taking trade secrets with them. While it has chiefly involved attacks by Apple, OpenAI has now made its own litigious move on the matter.

In its countersuit, the Financial Times reports, OpenAI claims that Apple has itself stolen trade secrets from it. Again, it involved employees moving from one company to the other.

This was something OpenAI has already claimed to the court in October. In that filing, an investigation prompted by the Apple trade secret lawsuit allegedly uncovered trade theft by Apple itself.

That filing said that the supposed thief joined OpenAI from Apple, worked for OpenAI for six months, then returned to Apple. On their return, the thief allegedly brought with them details of one OpenAI hardware device via their personal accounts.

The document trove apparently included images, engineering information, supplier details, manufacturing data, and standards for cosmetic finishes and sealants.

Anti-competitive

At the same time, OpenAI accuses Apple of using its size to stall competition, as OpenAI prepares its own AI devices for sale. This apparently involves Apple "coercing and threatening" suppliers who work both for Apple and for OpenAI.

To OpenAI, this is an attempt by Apple to "compete unfairly by any means available."

Apple is using its size and resources to "forestall competition" by threatening suppliers, both existing and potential ones. This involves a "wide variety of unlawful, unfair, and tortious conduct," the filing adds.

While Apple habitually locks in capacity from its supply chain members to keep production running smoothly, Apple apparently goes beyond that. Instead, it is claimed to be "coercing and threatening" suppliers who work with OpenAI on its hardware.

Hotel (Designed in) California

OpenAI also took a moment in the filing to complain about Apple's lawsuit, accusing it of really being an attempt to stop employee poaching.

It was claimed that Apple had encouraged employees to store corporate files on personal devices and cloud storage accounts. This became one way the trade secrets leaked out to OpenAI.

OpenAI describes it as a trap for employees. "Bright young minds thought they would work in Cupertino," the filing muses.

"Instead, they were joining Hotel California: you can check out any time you like, but you can never leave."

A statement from an Apple spokesperson shared with AppleInsider states:

"This case is about OpenAI employees deliberately stealing, accessing, and using Apple's secret and confidential information regarding our unreleased technologies, processes, and products — not about inadvertent retention of Apple information. OpenAI's counterclaims are a transparent attempt to distract from the substance of Apple's lawsuit, in which OpenAI has already been ordered to stop using Apple's confidential information."

The story so far

Apple sued OpenAI in July 2026, alleging former employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu took trade secrets to OpenAI after leaving Apple. OpenAI disputed Apple's claim that it ignored complaints, pointing to an email mixup involving Apple's lawyers.

OpenAI subsequently published an open letter defending its hires and sharing messages between Liu and former colleagues. It argued that departing employees could retain Apple files despite neither wanting them nor knowing they remained accessible.

The company's defense later focused on whether Apple adequately protected the information it described as trade secrets. Apple also accused OpenAI of introducing improper arguments as the companies fought over a preliminary injunction.

After convincing the court to grant access to some OpenAI documents, OpenAI then accused Apple of stealing trade secrets from it.

In October, OpenAI swore it won't use Apple's trade secrets at the heart of the lawsuit, after the judge said the court was "highly likely" to grant Apple's injunction. One that could stop OpenAI from working on its AI device.

Later that month, the judge granted more requests from Apple for information from OpenAI. That included devices used by ex-Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan used to store the information, messaging apps, AI tool usage, and any confidential Apple information that may have been destroyed.

As it stands, the actual courtroom fight between the companies will take place on July 19, 2027, starting at 9 A.M.

Updated November 27, 2026 at 7:11 PM Eastern: Added Apple statement.

items.title: Black Friday streaming deals deliver Disney Plus & Hulu for $4.99/mo
items.content_html:
Black Friday streaming deals have expanded to include a year of Disney+ and Hulu for $4.99 per month, with new discounts on HBO Max and Peacock joining existing Apple TV savings.

Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max, and Peacock have introduced discounts since our November 20 streaming roundup. Combining the new Disney+ and Hulu bundle with HBO Max's Black Friday promotion brings the cost of all three services to just $10.48 per month for an entire year.

Most of the major promotions run through Cyber Monday on November 30, although eligibility requirements and discounted subscription periods vary.

Disney+ & Hulu bundle gets a Black Friday discount

The ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu bundle deal cuts the monthly subscription from $12.99 to $4.99 per month for 12 months, saving subscribers $96 over the year.

Viewers who prefer ad-free streaming can get the Premium bundle for $14.99 per month instead of $21.99, saving $84 over the same period. Some live programming may still contain ads.

Both promotions are available through November 30 to new and eligible returning subscribers. Customers with active Disney+, Hulu, ESPN, or bundle subscriptions don't qualify.

Subscriptions automatically renew at the regular monthly price after the promotional period unless canceled.

HBO Max cuts subscription costs in half

HBO Max is offering its Basic with Ads plan for $5.49 per month for 12 months, down from $10.99. New and eligible returning subscribers can save $66 by claiming the promotion through November 30.

Customers who qualify for the Disney+/Hulu and HBO Max promotions streaming promotions can save more than 50% compared with the regular $21.99 monthly price of the ad-supported bundle containing Disney+, Hulu, and HBO Max. The separate subscriptions cost a combined $125.76 over the promotional year instead of $263.88 for the regular three-service bundle.

Apple TV remains more than half off

Apple's Black Friday streaming promotion cuts the cost of Apple TV from $14.99 to $6.99 per month for six months, saving subscribers $48.

Subscribers get access to original series such as Severance, Foundation, and Slow Horses, along with Major League Soccer and Friday Night Baseball coverage.

U.S. subscribers also get Formula 1 coverage, with Apple expanding its motorsports programming to include F1 Academy races in 2027.

New and eligible returning subscribers have until November 30 to claim the discount.

Peacock offers monthly & annual streaming discounts

Peacock is discounting monthly and annual subscriptions to its Select and Premium tiers after sitting out last year's Black Friday sales.

  • Peacock Select monthly - $2.99 per month for three months, down from $8.99.
  • Peacock Select annual - $29.99 for one year, down from $89.99.
  • Peacock Premium monthly - $8.99 per month for three months, down from $12.99.
  • Peacock Premium annual - $89.99 for one year, down from $129.99.

Both tiers contain ads, but the cheaper Select plan primarily includes television programming from NBC, Bravo, and other networks. Subscribers who want live sports, movies, or Peacock Originals will need the Premium plan.

The annual Select subscription offers the biggest percentage discount, saving customers $60 over the first year. New and eligible returning subscribers can claim the discounts through November 30.

Paramount+ discounts both subscription tiers

Paramount+ is still offering its Essential and Premium subscriptions for $2.99 per month for two months, down from $8.99 and $13.99, respectively.

Since both plans cost the same during the promotion, Premium offers better value with Showtime programming, offline downloads, and mostly ad-free on-demand streaming.

Streaming on Apple TV

New and eligible former subscribers can claim the discount through November 30. Premium subscribers will save $22 over two months, but they'll pay the higher monthly rate once the promotion expires.

Crunchyroll offers six months of discounted anime streaming

Anime fans can get Crunchyroll's Fan subscription for $3.99 per month for six months, down from $9.99. The Mega Fan subscription costs $5.99 per month for the same period instead of $13.99.

The promotions save Fan subscribers $36 and Mega Fan subscribers $48 over six months.

Starz offers a full year of discounted streaming

Starz remains one of the cheapest streaming subscriptions available this Black Friday, with a full year of access for $11.99 upfront instead of $69.99. A separate monthly promotion costs $2.99 per month for three months instead of $11.99.

Customers who choose the annual promotion will automatically switch to monthly billing at the prevailing rate after the first year unless they cancel. Starz currently charges $11.99 per month.

Amazon discounts Prime Video streaming subscriptions

Amazon's Black Friday streaming sale also offers savings of up to 75% on select Prime Video subscriptions and bundles, letting customers manage multiple streaming services through one account.

Previously advertised discounts include:

  • MGM+ - $1.99 per month for two months, down from $7.99.
  • AMC+ Premium - $2.75 per month for two months, down from $10.99.
  • BritBox - $2.75 per month for two months, down from $10.99.
  • PBS Masterpiece - $1.75 per month for two months, down from $6.99.
  • Hallmark+ - $2.25 per month for three months, down from $8.99.

Anyone taking advantage of multiple Black Friday streaming deals should check when each discount expires. Customers who sign up for two-month promotions during Black Friday could find themselves paying regular subscription prices as early as January 2027.

items.title: Black Friday iPhone deals go beyond $1,200 off with free Apple gear
items.content_html:
Black Friday iPhone deals offer up to $1,200 off Apple's latest smartphones, with AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon now bundling discounted or free Apple Watches and iPads with qualifying purchases.

All three carriers are offering ways to get the iPhone 18 Pro without monthly device payments. Promotions also extend to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, Apple's foldable iPhone Duo, and older models.

Carriers have been competing for customers since the iPhone 18 Pro launched, when we first covered carrier discounts reaching $1,200. Black Friday brings additional switching incentives and hardware bundles, although customers will generally need to maintain qualifying wireless plans for 36 months.

AT&T Black Friday iPhone deals

AT&T is offering new and existing customers the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro for $0 per month with an eligible trade-in. The promotion provides up to $1,200 in bill credits over 36 months.

Get AT&T Black Friday deals

Customers can also get up to $1,200 off the iPhone 18 Pro Max or iPhone Duo. Maximum savings require an eligible trade-in and AT&T Premium 2.0, Elite 2.0, or a qualifying legacy unlimited plan.

AT&T's Black Friday offers include a bundle with up to $1,900 in total savings. Qualifying customers can get an iPhone 18 Pro for $0 per month, a 40mm Apple Watch SE 3 for $0.99 per month, and a 128GB iPad (A16) for $3.99 per month.

The bundle requires an eligible trade-in valued at $230 or more and AT&T Premium 2.0 or higher. Separate service plans cost $10.99 per month for the watch and $20.99 for the iPad.

Shoppers without a phone to trade in have other options. AT&T is offering the 256GB iPhone 17 Pro for $9.99 per month when adding a qualifying new line, with an online promotion reducing the price to $4.43 per month.

The 256GB iPhone Air is also available for $0.99 per month through an eligible new-line promotion without a trade-in.

T-Mobile Black Friday iPhone deals

T-Mobile is advertising up to $1,200 off the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo through eligible trade-ins or when customers switch from another carrier.

Get T-Mobile Black Friday deals

Customers who transfer an eligible number and activate a new line can get the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro for $0 per month through 36 monthly bill credits. No trade-in is required, but the promotion requires an eligible Experience Beyond plan or qualifying T-Mix plan with three Picks.


T-Mobile is offering up to $1,200 off the iPhone 18 Pro

Picks are benefits customers select through T-Mobile's T-Mix plans, including device promotions, streaming services, and other perks. Customers must maintain the required Picks throughout the financing period to keep their promotional savings.

Qualifying T-Mix service for the $1,200 offer starts at $95 per month with AutoPay, plus taxes and fees. Existing customers can also qualify by trading in an eligible device in any condition on qualifying plans, although the credit depends on the model.

T-Mobile is also offering an iPhone 18 Pro, 40mm Apple Watch SE 3, and 128GB iPad (A16) without monthly device payments. Customers must transfer an eligible phone number, activate a new line on a qualifying T-Mix plan, and allocate three Picks to the iPhone promotion.

The Apple Watch requires a service plan starting at $15 per month, while the iPad requires one starting at $25 per month. Both prices include AutoPay discounts but exclude taxes and fees.

Customers who'd prefer a larger smartphone can get the iPhone 18 Pro Max for under $100 after bill credits when switching to an eligible T-Mix plan with three Picks.

The carrier's holiday deals also include up to $1,200 off the iPhone Duo, reducing its $1,999.99 starting price to $799.99 before taxes and other charges.

We previously covered the iPhone Duo's launch discounts, which included up to $1,000 off through T-Mobile and $1,200 through AT&T. T-Mobile warns that shipping times are longer than usual because of demand, but it'll honor the current promotion.

Several less expensive iPhones are also eligible for discounts through T-Mix.

  • iPhone 17 for $0 with an eligible number transfer and two Picks.
  • iPhone 17e for up to $350 off with a qualifying new line and one Pick.
  • iPhone Air for $0 with an eligible trade-in in any condition and three Picks.
  • iPhone 17 Pro for up to $930 off with an eligible trade-in in good condition and two Picks.
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max for $0 with an eligible trade-in in any condition and three Picks.

Families can get four 256GB iPhone 17e devices without monthly device payments when activating four new lines on T-Mix Standard and allocating four Picks. Customers only need to transfer one eligible phone number, and no trade-ins are required.

The four-line promotion costs $100 per month with AutoPay, plus taxes and fees. T-Mobile also charges a $35 connection fee per line under the promotion.

Verizon Black Friday iPhone deals

Verizon is offering up to $1,200 in bill credits on the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro through its Simplicity Plan with Simplicity Pro. Qualifying customers can get the phone without monthly device payments or a trade-in.

Get Verizon Black Friday deals

The promotion requires an eligible new or upgraded smartphone line and a 36-month device payment agreement. Simplicity Pro also allows customers to upgrade their iPhone after paying off 33% of their current device payment agreement, subject to the program's terms.

Starting on Black Friday, Verizon is bundling the iPhone 18 Pro with an Apple Watch Series 12 and iPad (A16). Customers can receive up to $600 in promotional credits per connected device over 36 months, with no additional device payments on qualifying configurations.

Apple's latest mainstream smartwatch features improved display durability and a new health sensor system capable of collecting more frequent heart rate measurements.

Both the watch and iPad require separate service plans starting at $20 per month each with AutoPay. Customers taking advantage of the entire bundle will pay at least $40 per month for the two connected device lines, excluding their smartphone service, taxes, and fees.


Verizon is offering up to $1,200 in bill credits on the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro

Customers enrolled in Verizon Loyalty can also avoid activation and upgrade fees, potentially saving up to $40 per device.

Shoppers can compare the available promotions through Verizon's holiday offers.

What to know before buying an iPhone on Black Friday

The biggest difference between these carrier promotions and a traditional retail discount is how customers receive their savings. Carriers generally distribute discounts across 36 monthly bill credits, and customers can lose remaining credits if they cancel service or no longer meet the promotional requirements.

Premium wireless plans, activation charges, taxes, and additional service lines can increase the total cost. A $1,200 discount might look attractive, but an expensive unlimited plan could offset some of the savings compared with a cheaper alternative.

The same applies to Apple Watch and iPad bundles. Paying $40 per month for two additional service lines adds up to $1,440 over three years, so shoppers who don't need cellular connectivity may save more with standalone hardware discounts.

Customers considering an older iPhone should also compare the hardware before choosing solely on price. Our model comparison explains the differences between the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro, including performance and camera improvements.

For customers already planning to stay with a carrier for three years, the discounts can substantially reduce the cost of upgrading. Buyers who want the freedom to change carriers sooner should compare the full 36-month cost rather than relying on the advertised savings alone.

items.title: iPhone 18 production will start months behind schedule for spring 2027 launch
items.content_html:
Apple's iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e are set to begin mass production in January 2027. This is months behind the expected October schedule still in time for a rumored February or March release.

Apple already released the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max alongside the iPhone Duo, but it isn't done yet. The iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e have long been tipped for a spring 2027 unveiling.

Reports have penciled in a narrower timeframe to February or March. And while Apple would usually have begun mass production by now, Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital says that won't happen for a few more weeks yet.

In a new post to the Chinese social network, the leaker says that production of the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e won't begin until New Year's Day, 2027. This is after it was originally planned to kick off in October.

That timeframe matches a previous report that said much the same. At the time, it was argued that display manufacturers were instead focusing on panels for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

No time for panic

While it's true that Apple would have been expected to begin producing iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e units by now, it's too early to be that concerned about delays. While it will be cutting things tight, Apple should still be able to stick to that Q1 2027 release timeframe.

AppleInsider understands that it is invariably the Pro and Pro Max models that sell in the greatest volumes immediately after launch. The shift over to non-Pro happens in the first few months of the new year.

With that in mind, Apple doesn't need to produce the same volume of iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e handsets for launch day as it would for its more popular models.

This would also explain Apple's decision to have display makers focus on the handsets it can sell today.

items.title: Apple faces another App Store antitrust fight, this time in Chile
items.content_html:
Apple is facing renewed pressure to open its iOS ecosystem as Chile pushes for alternative app stores and payment systems.

On Friday, Chile's competition regulator asked the country's antitrust court to fine Apple approximately $80 million over alleged anticompetitive practices. The regulator also seeks corrective measures addressing Apple's restrictions on app distribution and in-app payments on iOS.

Reuters reports Chile's National Economic Prosecutor's Office (FNE) alleges Apple has restricted competition in both areas since at least 2019. The proposed fine is equal to 30% of sales from products and services linked to the alleged violations during the investigated period.

The FNE argues that Apple's restrictions on sideloading and alternative app stores forced developers and consumers to rely on Apple's own App Store. Apple has argued that its restrictions are done for security reasons, but the FNE believes them to be unnecessary.

The regulator wants the court to require Apple to permit third-party app stores, sideloading, and alternative in-app billing systems. It also seeks to allow developers to include payment buttons that direct users to external payment systems without unnecessary barriers.

Apple already permits third-party app marketplaces in the European Union, Japan, and Brazil following regulatory intervention. However, only the European Union requires Apple to allow developers to distribute individual apps directly through their websites.

In October 2026, Australia's Federal Court ordered Apple to allow third-party app stores and end its anti-steering practices. Apple has until March 1, 2027, to implement the court-ordered changes.

items.title: How to set up your own Hotline server for macOS in 2026
items.content_html:
Hotline is a familiar name to old-school Mac users, and it has been resurrected by a series of new projects. Here's how to set up a server on your Mac, and keep the service running safely.

Social media is an ever-evolving landscape, with services quickly coming to life and just as quickly disappearing once better options become available. However, before everyone got infatuated with Facebook and MySpace, there were much smaller communities and other technologies at play.

Before modern-day social media, chat services dominated, and predating those were things like bulletin board systems (BBS), forums, chat clients like Internet Relay Chat (IRC) and AOL Instant Messenger (AIM).

One of those that existed in the pre-millennium days and got some traction in the Apple space was Hotline. Surprisingly, while other platforms from that time have effectively shut down, Hotline is still kept alive by its die-hard users.

Here's how to host your own modern Hotline server, and to get involved in vintage Mac messaging.

What is Hotline?

Hotline is a suite of tools used to operate a bulletin board system. While older tech enthusiasts will think about dialing into a BBS using a modem on a specific phone number, this was one that operated over a wider network using TCP/IP.

That is to say, you can connect to it over something like the Internet, instead of trying to connect to a specific phone number.

For you younger folks, Hotline is an early predecessor of Discord.

Starting to set up MobiusAdmin

In short, it allowed people to communicate with each other in real-time chats, to message each other directly, and to create message boards for communities. It also allowed people to share files with each other too.

As you would expect from the wild frontier of the early modern Internet, it enabled a wide range of interests, communities, and content-sharing groups to develop. Everything from legitimate use cases such as community building to more nefarious and darker uses.

That means things like sharing pirated software and music, along with more adult content. This content meant it became popular, and tracker sites would appear online to share servers and login credentials.

Unlike a modern peer-to-peer file-sharing system, Hotline relied on a client-server model. Trackers would act as directories of servers for users to connect to, and client software would be needed to actually access those listed servers.

A potted Hotline history

Hotline dates back to 1996, developed by Australian programmer Adam Hinkley. It was initially known as "hotwire" before getting the slightly more marketable name.

Hotline has a troubled history, including lawsuits with Redrock Holdings over the development of AppWarrior, a class library made by Hinkley. After Hinkley moved to Toronto to be part of Hotline Communications, the software company that published and distributed Hotline Connect, he then left the company after a disagreement.

During its time, Hotline Communications found an audience at major companies, including Apple Computer Australia.

Its peak was in the late 1990's, after online users deemed it to be a successor to IRC. This led to the creation of thousands of Hotline servers across the Internet, driven by file sharing.

Late in the decade, early peer-to-peer file-sharing systems gained in popularity and heralded the modern-day piracy era. Users moved away from Hotline, in favor of these newer systems that seemingly worked faster and didn't require connecting to a specific server.

The once-celebrated and weakened Hotline Communications insisted that there would be a second version of the Hotline suite in 2021. That effort never saw a release.

Modern-day Hotline

It's been decades since the rise and fall of Hotline. As such, the original clients have fallen behind with the rest of the tech industry, and are ideally run on older Apple systems.

We're not just talking Intel Macs here, as there are client downloads for Power PC too.

Hotline Navigator, a modern client for the Hotline protocol.

Thankfully, there are other options that exist for modern Macs, thanks to the development efforts by enthusiasts keen to keep Hotline alive.

For clients, a good example for those on Apple Silicon Macs would be Hotline Navigator. It's a clone that works with macOS 11 or later as a Universal binary, as well as iPadOS, iOS, Android, Linux, and Windows.

It does this while still being backward compatible with the original network.

Of course, browsing is only part of the experience. You can also set up your own Hotline server, even on Apple Silicon.

How to set up a Hotline server on an Apple Silicon Mac

Mobius is a cross-platform Hotline server from the same people behind Hotline Navigator.

Capable of providing chat, file transfers, bulletin boards, and user accounts, it offers the same features as other Hotline servers back in the day. It can also handle the task of registering the server with trackers.

Setting up shared files, banners, and login agreements for users in MobiusAdmin

The cross-platform bit means you can run it on more than just a Mac. If you have a Linux server, a spare Windows PC, a virtual machine, or even a Raspberry Pi, you can set it up on that.

That said, we are more interested in setting up the server on macOS alone. Thankfully, while there are command-line versions for Linux and Windows, there's a handy GUI-based version for macOS, called MobiusAdmin.

Warning: Before you go through setting up the server, remember that you should abide by local laws when it comes to operating the server. That includes content-related things like not hosting pirated content, and other things that could get you sued or arrested.

Operating a server is fine, just do so appropriately and legally.

  • Download MobiusAdmin from the project's GitHub repository. Download the latest version.
  • Once downloaded, open the DMG file, then drag MobiusAdmin to Applications.
  • Open MobiusAdmin. Gatekeeper will warn you about running applications downloaded from the Internet. Dismiss the message.
  • On opening, you'll be greeted by a wizard to set up the server. Click Get Started.
  • Type in your Server Name and click Next. This will appear on tracker listings, so it's best to get this right from the start.
  • You'll be asked to describe your server, again so people viewing trackers will know what the server is about. Click Next.
  • You'll be asked what folders on your Mac will be used for file-sharing. By default, your Public Folder will be used, but use Browse to find and create a file elsewhere on your Mac's storage, ideally away from other personal files.
  • There is the option to set up a Server Banner, namely a 468 by 60-pixel GIF or JPG that is shown when users connect. You can use the default "Welcome!" one, but click Choose Custom Image to add your own creation.
  • The Login Agreement is text that will be shown to users when they initially connect to the server. This should be filled out with rules that others should follow when using the server, as well as other need-to-know things about the server's community.
  • You'll be asked to set up the Network Settings, specifically the port you want to use if you don't want to use the default 5500, with 5501 used for file transfers. Remember which ports are used, so you can forward the ports from your network's router.
  • You may also want to click the Bonjour checkbox if you want the server to be advertised on your local network. This is a good idea if you want to use it locally and not to expose it to the wider Internet.
  • Step 8 of the massive setup process is for Tracker Registration. If you want to open the server up to the public, keep the toggle enabled and the checkmarks against the trackers you want to use, otherwise turn off the registration toggle.
  • Under News Settings, you can change how dates appear on the message board. You can also adjust the Post Separator here, changing what appears between posts.
  • For Connection Limits, you can set the maximum number of downloads, downloads per client, or maximum connections per IP address. If you don't want to set a limit, you can enter 0 for each one of these to leave it as unrestricted.
  • Next, you will be advised of two Default Accounts that are automatically set up, including an admin account with a simple default password and a passwordless guest account.
  • It is vital to use the admin password shown here to access the admin account once the server goes live, and to change the password as soon as possible.
  • The last page shows the main settings you have set up for the server, including the name, description, your file root, selected port, banner, and if Bonjour is enabled.
  • Once happy, click Finish to conclude without starting the server up, or Start Server to run the server immediately as configured.

Once you're finished, you're greeted by the main page for the Hotline server. It's split into two sides.

Completing the MobiusAdmin server setup.

The left contains granular settings you configured during the setup process. Use this to change the settings of the server, including its name, configured directory, port, logging, and limits.

The right section is where you make the main changes to the server. Under "Server," you can turn the server on and off, restart it, and run the setup wizard again.

The Accounts section allows you to manage the accounts attached to the server, including the guest account and admin. This also includes a section to manage what users are banned from accessing the server's contents.

Online gives you a live log of what users are connected, including IP addresses, and a log of what's happened on the server.

Files gives you a list of all of the accessible files in your shared directory that users can access. Lastly, News is the message board, accessible by users.

Safety and catches

We have already mentioned the legalities of hosting a publicly accessible file-sharing service. It is also worth remembering that doing so presents more dangers than just that.

Remember that you are effectively opening a port up through your router to a computer on your home network, for the purposes of file sharing. As always, this is an issue for the modern-day Internet, which is filled with various malicious software trying to gain access to any network it can.

Be very careful about doing this, and to make sure you have taken every precaution you can before welcoming anyone to your in-home server.

These precautions can include double-checking your router's port-forwarding and firewall rules. You may also want to check that your Mac's Firewall is turned on and configured correctly too, under System Settings, then Network.

As a server hosting files, you won't want it to be used that often. Opening your Mac to the dangers of the Internet at large is almost always a problem waiting to happen.

Managing users and viewing server logs in MobiusAdmin

Also, consider that it is an older file-sharing method. While it was previously maintained by a commercial entity, it's now being managed by a smaller group of individuals, who may not necessarily have the will or the time to fix absolutely every issue that surfaces.

With AI becoming both a help and a hindrance in the security field, this becomes an even bigger threat.

If you just want to operate the server for a small curated audience, turn off tracker registration. This effectively operates as a neon sign for Hotline users.

This ideally should be disabled during the initial setup, but you can also do so after the fact. Under the settings of the server, go to Tracker Registration and turn the toggle for Enable Tracker Registration off.

Keeping Bonjour enabled is a much smaller risk, but still something you can disable just in case.

However, if you're using it with a small group of friends, one of the more secure ways of using it is with a service like Tailscale. This funnels the connection through a virtual private network, so you can potentially keep it off the wider internet entirely.

Do enjoy experimenting with older software, but be careful at the same time.

items.title: Best video color grading software in 2026 includes Adobe Premiere
items.content_html:
Professional color grading software can make or break the look of a video, and Adobe Premiere gives everyone from novices to seasoned professionals the tools to achieve cinematic results.

Capturing the video you need for a project is only half of the battle. Sometimes the footage you capture matches your creative vision with minimal editing, but when it isn't quite right, color grading can get you the rest of the way.

While some entry-level video editing tools rely heavily on basic filters, professional color grading software provides greater control over color, contrast, exposure, and tonal adjustments.

Adobe Premiere has an extensive suite of color grading tools baked in, with much of the work accomplished using the dedicated Color Mode. Support for third-party plug-ins provides even more creative flexibility.

Get Adobe Premiere

You don't need years of video editing experience to get started with Adobe Premiere. At the same time, its color grading tools offer enough depth to accommodate demanding professional workflows.

Color Management and Color Mode

Recording video in RAW or using a log color profile can give you greater flexibility during post-production. Adobe Premiere's built-in Color Management system simplifies the process, while Color Mode provides the tools needed to fine-tune your footage.

Color grading can transform an ordinary shot into cinematic footage. Adobe Premiere gives you precise control over color, contrast, and exposure, helping you preserve detail while achieving your desired aesthetic.

If you've ever wondered exactly how a Western achieves its sepia tone or your favorite sci-fi film has those cold corridors, it's thanks to color grading. What's great is that Adobe Premiere gives you as much artistic control as you want through direct manipulation or presets.

You can even import your own presets to create a specific look. Built-in tools like Auto Color can automatically adjust exposure and white balance, giving you a starting point for further creative refinements without sacrificing artistic control.

The best video color grading software provides the tools you need while staying out of the way. Adobe Premiere's Color Mode supports HDR color grading workflows, while the Clip Grid makes it easy to compare shots, identify inconsistencies, and navigate between clips that need additional adjustments.

Basic tools are also key

Sometimes you just need to get in and get out before publishing your video to social media. Adobe Premiere offers quick export options and simple editing tools.

Even simple adjustments can improve your video

Easily adjust color temperature, exposure, saturation, and more, much like editing a photo. Make adjustments to individual clips or across an entire sequence.

Adobe Premiere also offers Styles, which combine multiple color adjustments to help you quickly achieve a cohesive look across your footage.

The built-in Style Browser is full of presets that can help you achieve your desired color grading effect.

If you've achieved the perfect look in one clip, Adobe Premiere lets you easily copy that color grade and apply it to another, helping maintain visual consistency throughout a project.

Color grading tool pricing

Adobe Premiere offers far more than color grading. Its inclusion in the Adobe Creative Cloud Pro subscription gives you access to a comprehensive video editing platform alongside other creative apps, including Photoshop and After Effects.

While free online color grading tools may be sufficient for basic adjustments, some have limited export settings and color management capabilities. Professional software like Adobe Premiere gives you greater control over both the appearance and output quality of your footage.

Adobe's Creative Cloud Pro subscription, which includes Premiere and more than 20 creative apps, normally costs $69.99 per month. During Adobe's Black Friday sale, the price drops to $29.99 per month for the first year, reflecting a 57% discount.

Eligible students and teachers can save even more, with first-year pricing of $15.99 per month. Both promotional rates require an annual subscription billed monthly, with the offers ending Nov. 27.

With Adobe's Black Friday discount, now is an excellent time to invest in professional video editing and color grading software. Get Adobe Premiere through Creative Cloud Pro.
